passage: Thursday. The whole team nodded through the new launch plan today. Tejas presented it with such confidence that saying anything felt rude. I had three worries: the timing, the budget and the vendor. I said nothing. Neither did anyone else, and Meera even said, "Love it." Afterwards at the water cooler Meera whispered, "Did anyone actually think this would work?" Then Sameer joined and said, "I was up all night worrying about the vendor." Almost everyone had doubts. Ten heads nodded and hardly one meant it. I felt oddly relieved and embarrassed at the same time. Tomorrow I will write my three worries down and send them to Tejas. — Divyansh

qa.q: What did Sameer say kept the night awake?
qa.a: Sameer said "I was up all night worrying about the vendor."

qa.q: What is Divyansh feeling after the water-cooler talk?
qa.a: Divyansh feels relieved that the doubts were shared and embarrassed that nobody said so in the meeting, a mixed state.

qa.q: What choice does Divyansh make for the next day?
qa.a: Divyansh decides to write the three worries down and send them to Tejas, which turns a private doubt into something that can be discussed.

qa.q: What might Meera be feeling, having said "Love it" and then whispering "Did anyone actually think this would work?"
qa.a: Meera probably feels uneasy and a little guilty, having agreed aloud while doubting, and relieved to find the others were unsure too.

grounding: A team nods through a plan while each person privately has worries, and hallway chats reveal that the unity was an illusion.

passage:
The Monday meeting at the Gurugram startup lasted twelve minutes. The founder showed the launch plan: new app in two weeks. “Any concerns?” Nobody spoke. Seven heads nodded. Devika nodded too, though the payment page still crashed on her phone.
In the pantry afterwards, she was stirring her coffee when Jeevan came in. He looked around, lowered his voice. “Two weeks? Honestly? The login bug isn't fixed.”
Devika blinked. “I thought I was the only one worried.”
Rhea, reaching for a mug, laughed without humour. “I'm worried about the servers.”
By lunchtime Devika had counted five out of seven who had doubts. The meeting had looked so united.

qa.q: How long did the Monday meeting last?
qa.a: It lasted twelve minutes.

qa.q: What was Devika feeling when she nodded in the meeting?
qa.a: She felt anxious and doubtful because the payment page still crashed, but kept it to herself when everyone else nodded.

qa.q: What could the team do now that they know about the doubts?
qa.a: They could ask the founder for a short follow-up meeting where each person lists one risk before the launch date is fixed.

qa.q: What is it like for Jeevan to find that others share his worry?
qa.a: He is probably relieved not to be alone, and maybe frustrated that everyone stayed silent in the meeting.

grounding: Shows a team nodding through a plan while each has private worries, revealed later in pantry chats as almost everyone's doubt.

passage:
“So, everyone agrees? Sports day moves to a Saturday, all staff come in,” the principal said. Every teacher nodded.
In the corridor afterwards, Keerthana caught up with Jahnavi.
“Did you actually agree?”
Jahnavi sighed. “No. I have my son's exam that Saturday. You?”
“I think half the parents work Saturdays. Who'll come?”
Mr Thomas walked past with a stack of notebooks. “You two also think it's a bad idea?”
“Also?” Keerthana said.
“Ms Bose said the same in the staffroom. And the PE teacher.”
Jahnavi laughed weakly. “So it was only unanimous in the room.”
“Should we tell her?”
They looked at each other.

qa.q: Which day did the principal want sports day moved to?
qa.a: Sports day moves to a Saturday.

qa.q: How did Jahnavi feel about the decision she had nodded to?
qa.a: Jahnavi felt worried and frustrated because of the son's exam that Saturday.

qa.q: What would you advise the teachers to do now?
qa.a: They could go to the principal together, calmly, and share their concerns, since most staff seem to have them.

qa.q: How might the principal see things if the teachers speak up?
qa.a: She might be surprised and a little concerned that her staff nodded without agreeing, but able to rethink before it's too late.

grounding: Shows a staff meeting nodding through a plan while each teacher privately doubts it, revealed in corridor chats.

passage:
I'm Imran, and I learned something about meetings last spring.
Our architecture firm was presenting the community centre design. The partner asked, “Are we all happy with the glass front?” Six of us nodded. I nodded, even though I thought the west-facing glass would turn the hall into an oven by afternoon.
After the meeting, Ojas and I walked to the lift. He said, very quietly, “That glass is going to cook people.”
I stopped. “You too?”
In the stairwell we ran into Nandini, who said she'd been worried about cleaning costs and heat. By evening we knew five of six had doubts.
We had all nodded. The unity in that room was only on our faces. I remember feeling foolish and oddly relieved at the same time.

qa.q: Which way did the glass front face?
qa.a: It faced west.

qa.q: How did Imran feel after learning the others had doubts?
qa.a: Imran felt foolish and oddly relieved at the same time, having thought the worry was private.

qa.q: What could the firm do differently in future meetings?
qa.a: The partner could ask each person to name one concern in turn, instead of asking if everyone is happy.

qa.q: How might Ojas have felt when he learned Imran shared his worry?
qa.a: He likely felt relieved and less alone, since he had spoken very quietly as if unsure it was allowed.

grounding: A young architect recalls a meeting where everyone nodded through a design while privately doubting it, an illusion of unity.

passage:
Observation note, product review, 14 March. Written by the programme coach.
The team approved Binita's plan to launch the payments feature in two weeks. Six people, six nods, no questions. Gautam, who built most of the backend, nodded too, though he tapped his pen the whole time and never looked up.
Afterwards I stood near the coffee machine. Gautam told Neel, "Two weeks is tight for testing." Neel said, "I thought so too." By the lift, Harpreet told a colleague she was worried about the support team. By evening I had heard some doubt from four of the six.
What I did next: I asked Binita to reopen the decision tomorrow with one change. Each person writes down the biggest risk before anyone speaks, and Binita gives her view last. I also told Gautam, privately and kindly, that I had noticed the pen.

qa.q: By evening, how many of the six had shared a doubt?
qa.a: Four of the six.

qa.q: What does Gautam's pen-tapping during the meeting suggest?
qa.a: Gautam was worried that two weeks was too short for testing but felt uncomfortable being the one to break a unanimous nod.

qa.q: How might the coach's change to tomorrow's meeting help?
qa.a: Writing risks first and hearing Binita last lets people state doubts before the leader's view sets the mood.

qa.q: How might Binita feel on learning four people had doubts?
qa.a: Binita might feel surprised and a little stung that nobody spoke up, but also relieved to hear it before the launch.

grounding: Shows a team nodding through a plan while nearly everyone privately doubts it, which only surfaces in hallway talk afterwards.
